frequency_tr_v1_depth_preference_001.notes: Early match messaging tone; depth vs light/brief trade-off preserved.
frequency_tr_v1_depth_preference_001.prompt_en: In early messaging with a new match, what kind of tone feels more comfortable to you?

options.A: After a light hello, I try to move into a topic I'm curious about.
options.B: I ask an everyday question and go deeper based on how they reply.
options.C: I open with something witty and surface-level.
options.D: I keep it short and wait for a better moment.

frequency_tr_v1_depth_preference_002.notes: Stuck on daily logistics; deepening vs staying practical vs exiting.
frequency_tr_v1_depth_preference_002.prompt_en: The conversation is stuck on everyday errands; how do you steer the topic?

options.A: I ask a question about why this topic matters.
options.B: I ask for a bit more detail while staying practical.
options.C: I keep the agenda as is and don't change the topic.
options.D: I cut the conversation short.

frequency_tr_v1_depth_preference_003.notes: Partner giving short replies; deepen / retry / match pace / defer.
frequency_tr_v1_depth_preference_003.prompt_en: Your partner keeps giving short replies; how do you continue?

options.A: I deepen the topic with an open-ended question.
options.B: I keep the pace and try one more angle.
options.C: I match their pace and stay brief.
options.D: I drop the topic and say we can talk another time.

frequency_tr_v1_depth_preference_004.notes: Calm ongoing chat; invite deeper thoughts vs light/practical/brief.
frequency_tr_v1_depth_preference_004.prompt_en: You've been messaging for a while and the mood is calm. How do you prefer to keep the conversation going?

options.A: I suggest moving past how the day went into thoughts that have been affecting them.
options.B: I keep it light and slowly drift into something a bit more personal when it fits.
options.C: I stay on practical topics and keep the flow going without going deeper.
options.D: I keep it short and plan to message again later.

frequency_tr_v1_depth_preference_005.notes: 1:1 chance from group chat; values/hobbies vs general/group flow.
frequency_tr_v1_depth_preference_005.prompt_en: A one-to-one chance opens up in a group chat; what do you choose to talk about?

options.A: I ask about a shared value or motivation.
options.B: I build a light but personal connection through hobbies.
options.C: I keep the group vibe and talk about general things.
options.D: I stay in the group flow instead of splitting off one-to-one.

frequency_tr_v1_social_energy_001.notes: Weekend hangout; full join / short visit / skip / propose 1:1.
frequency_tr_v1_social_energy_001.prompt_en: Your friends are organizing a small get-together this weekend; what's your preference?

options.A: If I'm feeling energetic, I join the whole gathering.
options.B: I stop by briefly and catch the enjoyable part.
options.C: I skip it this week and prefer to rest.
options.D: Instead of a group setting, I suggest a one-to-one plan.

frequency_tr_v1_social_energy_002.notes: Tired but invited; join / brief / skip / defer 1:1 away from crowd.
frequency_tr_v1_social_energy_002.prompt_en: A small get-together with people close to you is planned; you're tired but invited. What's your preference?

options.A: I gather my energy and join the get-together.
options.B: I come for a short while and plan to leave afterward.
options.C: I skip it this time and choose to rest.
options.D: I avoid the crowd and postpone a one-to-one meet-up.

frequency_tr_v1_social_energy_003.notes: New venue invite; join eagerly / go but leave early / stay home / quieter alt.
frequency_tr_v1_social_energy_003.prompt_en: Your friend group suggests going to a new place; what do you do?

options.A: I join right away and enjoy exploring a new setting.
options.B: I go, but I might plan to leave early.
options.C: I prefer to stay home.
options.D: Instead of a crowded place, I suggest a quieter alternative.

frequency_tr_v1_social_energy_005.notes: Date venue energy gradient: lively → mid → quiet walk → private.
frequency_tr_v1_social_energy_005.prompt_en: A new match suggests meeting up; what's your preference for the setting?

options.A: I suggest a lively café or a busy place.
options.B: I suggest a medium-paced, comfortable place.
options.C: I prefer a quiet walk or a park.
options.D: I prefer meeting at home or somewhere secluded.

frequency_tr_v1_social_energy_007.notes: Partner wants quiet after busy week; you feel rested — light invite vs space.
frequency_tr_v1_social_energy_007.prompt_en: After a busy week your partner wants quiet time, but you feel rested. What do you do?

options.A: Even while respecting their need, I offer a light social suggestion.
options.B: I send a short voice note and then leave them space.
options.C: I accept the quiet and spend time on my own.
options.D: I pull back fully and keep contact to a minimum for a while.

frequency_tr_v1_spontaneity_001.notes: Sudden Friday invite; accept now vs think vs postpone vs refuse spontaneous.
frequency_tr_v1_spontaneity_001.prompt_en: You have no plans for Friday evening; someone suddenly suggests hanging out. What's your preference?

options.A: I accept right away and figure out the plan in the moment.
options.B: I think briefly and say yes if it works.
options.C: I prefer planning ahead, so I postpone.
options.D: I usually turn down last-minute invitations.

frequency_tr_v1_spontaneity_002.notes: Planned activity vs new idea mid-day; flex vs stick to plan.
frequency_tr_v1_spontaneity_002.prompt_en: You had a plan for a shared activity; a new idea comes up during the day. What's your preference?

options.A: I say we should loosen the plan and try the new idea right away.
options.B: After a quick check, I change direction.
options.C: I stick with the original plan.
options.D: I avoid last-minute changes and keep the schedule.

frequency_tr_v1_spontaneity_003.notes: Open weekend + friend suggests different activity; try vs evaluate vs hold vs avoid change.
frequency_tr_v1_spontaneity_003.prompt_en: You don't have a firm weekend plan; a friend suggests a different activity. What do you do?

options.A: I switch to the new plan right away and enjoy trying it.
options.B: After a quick check, I accept if it works.
options.C: I stick with what I already had in mind.
options.D: I avoid last-minute changes.

frequency_tr_v1_spontaneity_006.notes: Weeknight plan set; last-minute alt — drop plan vs small tweak vs stick vs refuse.
frequency_tr_v1_spontaneity_006.prompt_en: Your weekday evening plan is set; someone suggests something different at the last minute. What do you do?

options.A: I drop the plan and accept the new suggestion.
options.B: If it works, I can make a small change.
options.C: I stick with the plan we already agreed on.
options.D: I usually turn down last-minute changes.

frequency_tr_v1_spontaneity_007.notes: New match suddenly proposes different meet time; adapt vs check vs hold vs avoid.
frequency_tr_v1_spontaneity_007.prompt_en: A new match suddenly suggests a different meeting time. What's your preference?

options.A: I adapt right away and accept the new time.
options.B: I reply quickly based on my availability.
options.C: I prefer sticking to the time we already set.
options.D: I avoid sudden time changes.

frequency_tr_v1_stability_001.notes: Weekly meet habit with new person; fixed rhythm vs frame vs variable vs no fixed plan.
frequency_tr_v1_stability_001.prompt_en: When it comes to building a weekly meet-up habit with someone you just met, what's your preference?

options.A: I suggest a regular rhythm on the same day/time each week.
options.B: I set a general frame and we clarify the details together.
options.C: I'm open to moving at a different pace each week.
options.D: I leave it to the flow without making a fixed plan.

frequency_tr_v1_stability_002.notes: Unset early communication rhythm; propose cadence vs frame vs variable vs flow.
frequency_tr_v1_stability_002.prompt_en: Your communication rhythm with someone you just met hasn't settled yet. What's your preference?

options.A: I suggest a weekly repeating meet-up or chat rhythm.
options.B: I set a general frame and clarify the details together.
options.C: I'm open to moving at a different pace each week.
options.D: I leave it to the flow without making a fixed plan.

frequency_tr_v1_stability_004.notes: Settled daily routine vs other's different tempo; protect vs tweak vs try vs hold own.
frequency_tr_v1_stability_004.prompt_en: Your daily routine is settled; someone you've met suggests a different pace. What's your preference?

options.A: I keep my current routine and don't change it beyond small adjustments.
options.B: I can make small adjustments that still fit my routine.
options.C: I'm open to a pace change and willing to try it.
options.D: Rather than disrupt my routine, I continue at my own pace.

frequency_tr_v1_stability_005.notes: Long-term rhythm disrupted; restore vs update vs adapt vs abandon fixed rhythm.
frequency_tr_v1_stability_005.prompt_en: Your long-term communication rhythm is settled; an unexpected change comes up. What do you do?

options.A: I try to return to the previous rhythm as soon as possible.
options.B: I propose an updated rhythm based on the new conditions.
options.C: I accept the change and adapt to the new pace.
options.D: I leave it to the natural flow without looking for a fixed rhythm.

frequency_tr_v1_stability_006.notes: Partner was quiet; reconnection — restore cadence vs light check-in vs try new tempo vs flow.
frequency_tr_v1_stability_006.prompt_en: Your partner has been quiet for a while; a chance to reconnect comes up. What's your preference?

options.A: I propose rebuilding the earlier regular contact rhythm.
options.B: I suggest a light but predictable check-in pattern.
options.C: I stay flexible this time and say we'll try a new pace.
options.D: I trust the natural flow without setting a rhythm.

frequency_tr_v1_disclosure_pace_001.notes: Personal disclosure with new match; early open vs gradual vs general vs wait for trust.
frequency_tr_v1_disclosure_pace_001.prompt_en: When it comes to sharing personal information with a new match, what's your preference?

options.A: Even early on, I share my basic expectations clearly.
options.B: I open up gradually as mutual trust builds.
options.C: I stay general and don't give personal details.
options.D: I don't open personal topics until trust has formed.

frequency_tr_v1_disclosure_pace_002.notes: Past relationships topic as trust starts; open early vs frame vs general vs withhold.
frequency_tr_v1_disclosure_pace_002.prompt_en: Trust is starting to build; past relationships come up. What's your preference?

options.A: I share my own experiences openly and early.
options.B: I give a basic frame and open the details gradually.
options.C: I stay general and don't give concrete examples.
options.D: I keep personal history private until trust is fully there.

frequency_tr_v1_disclosure_pace_003.notes: Personal topic arises mid-chat; share example vs slow details vs general vs change topic.
frequency_tr_v1_disclosure_pace_003.prompt_en: The conversation with a new match is progressing; a personal topic comes up. What do you do?

options.A: I share a short but clear example from my own experience.
options.B: I open the topic but release the details slowly.
options.C: I stay general and don't give a personal example.
options.D: I change the topic and wait until we know each other better.

frequency_tr_v1_disclosure_pace_005.notes: Reconnecting after silence; open status vs light note vs general hello vs defer personal.
frequency_tr_v1_disclosure_pace_005.prompt_en: Your partner has been quiet for a while; when reconnecting, how do you handle personal sharing?

options.A: I reopen the conversation by sharing my own situation clearly.
options.B: I share a light personal note and gauge the pace.
options.C: I continue with a general hello and don't give personal details.
options.D: After a silence, I put personal topics off for later.

frequency_tr_v1_disclosure_pace_006.notes: Moving from group meet to 1:1; early expectations vs light personal vs general vs defer.
frequency_tr_v1_disclosure_pace_006.prompt_en: You'll continue one-to-one with someone you met in a group setting; how do you handle personal sharing?

options.A: In the shift to one-to-one, I share my basic expectations early.
options.B: I share light personal information and gauge the pace.
options.C: I stay on general topics and don't give personal details.
options.D: Even one-to-one, I put personal topics off for later.

frequency_tr_v1_communication_pace_001.notes: Early messaging frequency; several short / AM-PM / wait for them / reply when free.
frequency_tr_v1_communication_pace_001.prompt_en: In the first days with a new match, what's your preference for how often you message?

options.A: I keep contact alive with a few short messages during the day.
options.B: I write regularly but in moderation, around morning and evening.
options.C: I usually wait until they write first.
options.D: I only reply briefly when it works for me.

frequency_tr_v1_communication_pace_002.notes: Long-term messaging rhythm; daily short contact vs flexible vs multi-day gaps vs long silence OK.
frequency_tr_v1_communication_pace_002.prompt_en: The relationship has progressed; what's your preference for a longer-term messaging rhythm?

options.A: I keep up regular short contact during the day.
options.B: I stay flexible but predictable based on the week's intensity.
options.C: I may go quiet for a few days and then catch up.
options.D: Long silences don't bother me.

frequency_tr_v1_communication_pace_003.notes: Partner silent a few hours; nudge vs end-of-day vs wait vs treat silence as normal.
frequency_tr_v1_communication_pace_003.prompt_en: Your partner hasn't written for a few hours; you're not free but you're curious. What do you do?

options.A: I send a short message and hope the flow continues.
options.B: I plan a wrap-up message for the end of the day.
options.C: I wait until they write and don't reach out if it isn't urgent.
options.D: I treat a longer silence as normal and don't message.

frequency_tr_v1_communication_pace_005.notes: Established daily habit; every day vs weekday regular vs as-needed vs long gaps OK.
frequency_tr_v1_communication_pace_005.prompt_en: You've known each other for a while; what's your usual daily communication habit?

options.A: We definitely message at least once every day.
options.B: Weekdays are regular; weekends can be more sparse.
options.C: I write when needed and don't look for a fixed rhythm.
options.D: Long gaps don't worry me.

frequency_tr_v1_communication_pace_007.notes: Friday plan unclear; dense messaging vs few clear msgs vs stay quiet vs minimize.
frequency_tr_v1_communication_pace_007.prompt_en: Friday evening plans aren't clear yet; how should last-minute messaging go?

options.A: I message frequently and try to decide quickly.
options.B: I narrow the options with a few clear messages.
options.C: I stay quiet until a decision is made.
options.D: If the plan is unclear, I keep messaging to a minimum.

frequency_tr_v1_depth_preference_007.notes: During shared activity; talk meaning vs check feelings vs keep light vs do quietly together.
frequency_tr_v1_depth_preference_007.prompt_en: You're going to try a new activity together; what's your preference on the conversation side?

options.A: I like talking about what the experience means while we're doing it.
options.B: I check in on feelings now and then, but mostly stay focused on the activity.
options.C: I focus on the activity and keep conversation light.
options.D: I prefer doing it together quietly.

frequency_tr_v1_depth_preference_008.notes: Personal topic as trust builds; go to roots vs mid-depth example vs practical vs defer.
frequency_tr_v1_depth_preference_008.prompt_en: Trust is starting to build; a personal topic opens up. What's your preference for conversation depth?

options.A: I want to go into the roots of the topic and explore the connections.
options.B: I stay in the middle and continue with a concrete example.
options.C: I tie the topic to practical outcomes.
options.D: I close the topic and say we can talk later.

frequency_tr_v1_communication_pace_004.notes: Coordinating activity by message; frequent updates vs few clear / reduce / prefer in person.
frequency_tr_v1_communication_pace_004.prompt_en: You're planning a new activity together; what's your style of coordinating by message?

options.A: I message often and share real-time updates.
options.B: I lock in the plan with a few clear messages and write when needed.
options.C: Once the plan is clear, I cut back on messaging.
options.D: I prefer talking face to face instead of by phone.

frequency_tr_v1_communication_pace_006.notes: After group meet, 1:1 messaging tempo; same day / next day / wait / natural opening.
frequency_tr_v1_communication_pace_006.prompt_en: You'll continue one-to-one with someone you met in a group setting; what's the messaging tempo?

options.A: After we part, I send a few messages the same day.
options.B: I continue the next day with a short message.
options.C: I usually wait until they write first.
options.D: I stay quiet for a while and wait for a natural opening.

frequency_tr_v1_social_energy_004.notes: Activity may be crowded; enjoy crowd / quieter corner / seek quieter alt / alone or leave early.
frequency_tr_v1_social_energy_004.prompt_en: You're going to try a new activity together; the setting may be crowded. What's your preference?

options.A: I enjoy spending time together in a crowded setting.
options.B: I join, but I prefer spending time in a quieter corner.
options.C: Instead of a crowd, I look for a more secluded alternative.
options.D: In a crowded setting I prefer being alone or leaving early.

frequency_tr_v1_social_energy_006.notes: Mid energy + weekend friend plans; full join / partial / skip / propose 1:1.
frequency_tr_v1_social_energy_006.prompt_en: You have weekend plans with friends; your energy is medium. What do you do?

options.A: I join the whole plan and try to build up my energy.
options.B: I join part of the plan and leave afterward.
options.C: I skip it this time and make time for myself.
options.D: Instead of the group, I suggest meeting one-to-one.

frequency_tr_v1_spontaneity_004.notes: Group hangout someone suggests switching activity; try now vs discuss vs stick vs avoid group pivot.
frequency_tr_v1_spontaneity_004.prompt_en: At a group get-together, someone suggests switching to a different activity. What's your preference?

options.A: I say we should try the new suggestion right away.
options.B: After a short discussion, we change if it works.
options.C: I stick with the original plan.
options.D: I avoid sudden changes within the group.

frequency_tr_v1_spontaneity_005.notes: Mid-activity new idea; switch route vs evaluate vs continue vs avoid mid-change.
frequency_tr_v1_spontaneity_005.prompt_en: While doing an activity together, a new idea comes up; what's your preference?

options.A: We try the new idea right away and change the route.
options.B: After a quick check, we try it if it works.
options.C: I continue with the plan we started.
options.D: I avoid changing the plan mid-activity.

frequency_tr_v1_stability_003.notes: Weekend plan changed several times; constrain vs flexible frame vs adapt vs wait until clear.
frequency_tr_v1_stability_003.prompt_en: The weekend plan has changed several times; how do you approach it?

options.A: I propose a clear plan frame and limit the changes.
options.B: I stay flexible but try to keep the main frame.
options.C: I adapt to the changes and move to the new plan.
options.D: I avoid constantly changing plans and wait until things are clear.

frequency_tr_v1_stability_007.notes: Weekly routine disrupted after group hangout; restore next day vs one-day flex vs stay flexible vs no need for routine.
frequency_tr_v1_stability_007.prompt_en: After a group get-together, your weekly routine is disrupted; what's your preference?

options.A: I make a point of returning to my routine the next day.
options.B: I flex for a day and then return to the routine.
options.C: If the routine is broken, I stay flexible for a while.
options.D: I don't feel a need for routine and leave it to the flow.

frequency_tr_v1_disclosure_pace_004.notes: Family/close circle topic as trust grows; open share vs frame vs surface vs later.
frequency_tr_v1_disclosure_pace_004.prompt_en: Trust is growing; the topic of family or close circle comes up. What do you do?

options.A: I share my own family/circle experiences openly.
options.B: I give a general frame and release the details slowly.
options.C: I keep the topic surface-level and don't give personal details.
options.D: I prefer opening these topics once we know each other better.

frequency_tr_v1_disclosure_pace_008.notes: Future plans/expectations once trust formed; concrete early vs frame vs general vs when clearer.
frequency_tr_v1_disclosure_pace_008.prompt_en: Trust has formed; future plans and expectations are being discussed. What's your preference?

options.A: I share my own expectations clearly and concretely.
options.B: I give a basic frame and open the details gradually.
options.C: I stay general and don't share concrete expectations.
options.D: I share future plans once they're clearer.

freq_separator_depth_comm_v1.prompt_en: You have recently met someone you like. Which communication pattern would feel most natural to you over the next week?

options.A: I would exchange frequent short messages during the day and leave deeper conversations for later.
options.B: I would communicate less often, but when we talk I would prefer longer and deeper conversations.
options.C: I would balance brief daily contact with an occasional longer conversation.
options.D: I would keep communication light and occasional until we know each other better.

freq_separator_social_stability_v1.prompt_en: When you have a free weekend, how do you usually prefer to arrange your social plans?

options.A: Having several different plans one after another tends to energize me.
options.B: One planned get-together and keeping the rest of the time for myself suits me better.
options.C: I prefer deciding who to see and what to do based on how I feel that day.
options.D: I mostly prefer my own space and may add a short social plan if I feel like it.

freq_separator_spontaneity_stability_v1.prompt_en: When planning a day together, which approach feels most natural to you?

options.A: I prefer settling the plan in advance and sticking to it as much as possible.
options.B: I like having a clear main plan while leaving room for small changes.
options.C: A rough idea is enough; I enjoy deciding the details during the day.
options.D: It feels more natural to decide most things at the last minute based on what we feel like doing.

freq_separator_disclosure_depth_v1.prompt_en: Someone you have recently started getting close to asks you a personal question early on. Which response is closest to you?

options.A: If I feel comfortable, I answer openly and in detail.
options.B: I share part of it and leave the more personal parts until trust develops.
options.C: I can talk about it, but I prefer more time before sharing personal details.
options.D: I prefer keeping the conversation lighter and building closeness through shared experiences first.

freq_separator_comm_stability_v1.prompt_en: When your messaging rhythm with someone close to you has been different from usual for a few days, what do you generally do?

options.A: I keep my usual communication rhythm and do not immediately read too much into the change.
options.B: I adjust how often I message to match their new rhythm.
options.C: At an appropriate time, I directly ask whether our communication rhythm is working for both of us.
options.D: I give the interaction some space to find its rhythm naturally again.

freq_separator_social_disclosure_v1.prompt_en: In a social setting where you feel comfortable, which pattern is usually closest to you?

options.A: I talk with many people but mostly keep the topics light.
options.B: I have longer conversations with fewer people and open up gradually.
options.C: I move between different people and may discuss personal topics when trust develops.
options.D: I observe the setting first and join one or two conversations once I feel comfortable.

freq_quality_instruction_v1.prompt_en: This item only checks whether the instruction was read and does not affect your profile. Please select “I read the instruction.”

options.A: I can continue
options.B: I read the instruction
options.C: I am unsure
options.D: I will answer later

freq_quality_protocol_v1.prompt_en: This is another short check that does not contribute to your profile score. For this item, please select “Continue.”

options.A: Wait a moment
options.B: Skip
options.C: Continue
options.D: Go back
